claims.text: Nanoscale chemical and lattice distortions govern strong low-field magnetocaloric response in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
The distortions produce nanoscale regions with enhanced local magnetic exchange.
These magnetically heterogeneous regions facilitate rapid magnetic entropy change with low hysteresis.
The high-entropy matrix maintains robust thermal conductivity and mechanical stability.
The baseline alloy is a single-phase disordered solid solution with slight nanoscale compositional variations and associated lattice distortions.
Composition tuning or controlled thermal treatment can accentuate or diminish chemical short-range order and associated lattice distortions.
Local compositional and lattice inhomogeneities generate spatial variations in magnetic exchange interactions.
Variations in magnetic exchange promote enhanced spin fluctuations and reversible magnetic ordering under low applied fields.
Enhanced spin fluctuations and reversible magnetic ordering produce a pronounced low-field magnetocaloric effect with low hysteresis.
The high-entropy structure provides efficient thermal pathways and mechanical integrity.
Increasing nanoscale heterogeneity relative to the baseline will increase the low-field isothermal entropy change.
Increasing nanoscale heterogeneity relative to the baseline will lower magnetic hysteresis.
Suppressing local distortions through homogenization or composition tuning will reduce the magnetocaloric response.
Suppressing local distortions will increase magnetic hysteresis.
The proposed behavior is limited to single-phase disordered FCC or BCC high-entropy alloys in refrigeration-relevant temperature and field ranges.
Phase-separated or extremely homogenized alloys may not exhibit the predicted relationship.
Rapid cooling or an alloying step can enhance chemical short-range order and lattice distortions relative to extended annealing.
Extended annealing can homogenize the microstructure and suppress nanoscale chemical and lattice inhomogeneities.
